stories.title: Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Fauci in contempt
stories.summary: The Senate Homeland Security Committee has voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress due to his refusal to answer questions during a recent hearing. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment over 100 times while addressing inquiries related to his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. This contempt finding may lead to further investigations regarding the validity of his constitutional rights against self-incrimination.

stories.title: FIFA Leadership Reaffirms Support for Infantino After Crisis Meeting
stories.summary: FIFA held a crisis meeting in Morocco where officials expressed their full support for President Gianni Infantino, despite recent controversies surrounding a failed proposal to allow private investment in the World Cup. The organization also issued an apology for the mistakes made during the planning process. Infantino's leadership appears secure for now, as the board aims to move forward from the backlash.

stories.title: Russian Attacks on Kyiv Highlight Ukraine's Air Defense Shortages
stories.summary: Recent Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv resulted in at least 17 fatalities and numerous injuries, exposing significant gaps in Ukraine's air defense capabilities. Despite intercepting many drones, Ukraine's air force reported that none of the incoming missiles were stopped, underscoring the urgent need for additional interceptor systems. The attacks have intensified, with the situation described as critical for civilian safety.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Six in Kharkiv and Sumy Regions, Damage Ship
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine resulted in the deaths of at least six people, with three fatalities reported in Balakliia, Kharkiv, and three in the Sumy region. Additionally, a foreign-flagged ship carrying wheat was damaged in the Black Sea area due to the attacks, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Abdul El-Sayed Secures Michigan Senate Primary Victory, Facing Republican Challenger
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed has won the Democratic primary for the Michigan Senate seat, defeating moderate Haley Stevens. This victory is seen as a significant win for the progressive wing of the Democratic Party and may influence the party's strategy heading into the November midterms. El-Sayed will now face Republican Congressman Mike Rogers in the general election.

stories.title: Violence in Southern Lebanon Claims Three Lives Amid Ongoing Tensions
stories.summary: Recent violence in southern Lebanon has resulted in the deaths of three individuals, including two Israeli soldiers, marking the first military fatalities for Israel in over a month. The Israeli military confirmed that the soldiers were killed by an explosion, prompting retaliatory strikes in the region. Lebanese authorities reported that one person was killed in these strikes, amidst ongoing US-backed negotiations aimed at reducing hostilities.

stories.title: Mohamed Salah Joins Trabzonspor on Two-Year Deal
stories.summary: Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year contract with Turkish club Trabzonspor after leaving Liverpool, where he spent nine years. During his time at Liverpool, Salah scored 257 goals in 442 appearances and won two Premier League titles and a Champions League trophy. His new contract reportedly includes a salary of 17 million euros per season.

stories.title: Explosive Drone Discovered Near Ukrainian Plane at German Airport
stories.summary: An explosives-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig Airport, prompting a counterterrorism investigation by German authorities. The drone was discovered by an airport employee near the south runway, and it contained an unknown explosive device. This incident is being treated as a potential hybrid attack scenario, raising concerns about new threats to aviation security.

The lawsuit was filed on the same day that New Mexico released a report detailing preliminary findings from its ongoing probe into Epstein's activities at a ranch in Stanley.

stories.title: DR Congo Faces Rapid Resurgence of Ebola Epidemic
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is grappling with a significant resurgence of Ebola, having recorded nearly 4,000 confirmed cases and over 1,800 deaths. This outbreak, attributed to the Bundibugyo virus, is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history and the fastest-spreading in the country's records.

stories.title: Mexican Influencer César Gastélum Killed During Live Stream
stories.summary: César Gastélum, a popular Mexican social media influencer, was shot and killed while live streaming outside a fast-food restaurant in Culiacán, Sinaloa. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening, and Gastélum had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok, where he was known for his comedy videos. He was reportedly attacked by a motorbike driver while filming with two friends.

stories.title: Nigerian Security Forces Conduct Major Rescue Operation, Free Over 300 Kidnapped Victims
stories.summary: Nigerian security forces have successfully rescued more than 300 individuals who were kidnapped, including 163 from a single village earlier this year. This operation is reported to be the largest single-day hostage recovery in the country's history, involving a joint effort by the military, police, and counter-terrorism units. The rescue took place in the Kainji Lake national park area, a region known for its dense forests where many victims were held captive.

stories.title: France to Implement Ban on Unsolicited Telemarketing Calls Next Week

The legislation seeks to shield vulnerable individuals from intrusive sales tactics and fraudulent practices. Violators of the ban could face fines of up to €75,000 per illegal call.
